steps.prompt: What are the three clues the speaker gives?
options: What you do with it, what it looks like, and what kind of thing it is.
The price you paid, the shop you bought it in, and the colour.
Where it comes from, who made it, and how old it probably is.
steps.answer: What you do with it, what it looks like, and what kind of thing it is.
steps.why: Function, appearance and category — those three almost always get you the word.

steps.title: Explaining a word you don’t know
steps.html:
The clue you giveWhat you say
you don’t know the wordI don’t know the word in English. / I’ve forgotten the word.
what kind of thing it isIt’s a kind of bag. / It’s a thing which you put into the wall.
what you do with itYou use it to record things. / It’s used for cutting cheese.
what it looks likeIt looks like a mobile phone. / It’s long and thin, like a stick.
what it’s made ofIt’s made of metal.
checking the listenerDo you know what I mean? / What’s it called?
when they get itExactly! That’s what I’m looking for!

It’s a kind of + noun puts the thing in a category the listener already knows.

You use it to + base verb, or It’s used for + -ing: You use it to cut cheese = It’s used for cutting cheese.

It looks like + noun compares it to something familiar. Do not say It looks like round — use It’s round.

This is the relative-clause pattern from Lesson 5, used for real: a thing which you put into the wall.

The complaint half of this lesson gives you phrases you will need again in Unit 10, Lesson 30, in a restaurant.

steps.title: Complaint email · model
steps.sub: A formal complaint email asking for a refund. You will write your own at the end.
steps.html:
Wrong item received

Subject: Order 41-88203 — wrong item received

Dear Sir or Madam,

I’m writing to complain about an order I received from you on 3 October (order number 41-88203).

I ordered a large black leather bag. The bag I received is a small blue plastic one, and one of the handles is broken. It is clearly not in a condition I can use, and it is not the item on your website.

I’d like a refund of the full amount, including the delivery fee. If a refund is not possible, please send me the correct bag this week.

I look forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,

A. Sarsenova

steps.title: Write a complaint email about something you bought.
steps.sub: About 90–120 words. Follow the model: greeting, why you are writing, what went wrong, what you want, sign-off.
steps.html:
• Dear Sir or Madam,
  • I’m writing to complain about …
  • I ordered … but the item I received is …
  • It is not in a condition I can use.
  • I’d like a refund of …
  • I look forward to your reply.
  • Yours faithfully,
Dear Sir or MadamI’m writing to complain aboutI orderedI receivedconditionbrokennot suitableI’d like a refundthe delivery feeI look forward to your replyYours faithfully
steps.modelHtml:
• I began with a greeting and ended with Yours faithfully.
  • I said in the first line why I was writing.
  • I said what I ordered and what actually arrived.
  • I said clearly what I want the company to do.
  • I did not use any informal phrases.
